claims.summary: バイキング is a Japanese abbreviation of バイキング料理; the word also has other dictionary senses, including historical Vikings, so context distinguishes them.
バイキング料理 is described as several dishes presented together for diners to serve themselves; the Japanese fixed-price model is described as all-you-can-eat.

The name バイキング料理 originated with the Imperial Hotel restaurant インペリアルバイキング in 1958, inspired by smörgåsbord; Imperial Hotel says the restaurant name became an expression associated with 食べ放題 in Japan.
The encyclopedia records 中華バイキング, 和食バイキング, 朝食バイキング and ケーキバイキング as format names.
The cited dictionaries and hotel history do not establish a universal rule distinguishing how every establishment uses バイキング, ビュッフェ and 食べ放題.
